name: Citizenship by Marriage

requirement_groups.name: Foreign wife of Syrian man, Arab/Syrian-origin background

requirements.blocker_text: Article 18 allows a foreign wife of a Syrian man to acquire Syrian nationality if she expresses a desire to do so AND holds Arab nationality, Syrian origin, or previously held Syrian nationality herself. Article 19 extends this to non-Arab women of Syrian origin. This is NOT a general route open to any foreign wife regardless of background -- the Arab/Syrian-origin condition is a real gate, not a formality.
requirements.fix_path: Submit a formal request expressing the desire to acquire nationality, evidencing the required Arab/Syrian-origin background.

requirement_groups.name: Wife of a foreign man naturalized as Syrian

requirements.blocker_text: Article 8: the wife of a foreign man who himself naturalized as Syrian may acquire nationality after application to the Ministry, at least 2 years of valid marriage, and legal residence, followed by ministerial decree approval. This is discretionary, not automatic.
requirements.fix_path: Apply to the Ministry after 2 years of marriage to a naturalized-Syrian husband, maintaining legal residence throughout.

evidence_required.document: Proof of Arab nationality / Syrian origin / prior Syrian nationality (first group only)
Proof of legal residence and 2 years' marriage (second group only)

sources.title: MENA Rights Group -- hosted English translation of Syria's Nationality Act (Legislative Decree No. 276 of 1969): Articles 8, 18, 19 (wife-side acquisition routes) and Article 12 (Syrian women's own nationality retention when married to a foreigner)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Syria). STATUS: DRAFT -- same tier-2 NGO-hosted-translation limitation as sy_citizenship_by_descent.json. ONE OF THE MOST TOTAL GENDER ASYMMETRIES FOUND IN THIS DATASET: there is NO mechanism anywhere in the Act's marriage provisions for a foreign husband of a Syrian woman to acquire Syrian nationality through the marriage. Article 12 addresses only the Syrian wife's own nationality -- she keeps it automatically unless she affirmatively chooses to take her foreign husband's nationality instead -- but nothing in the Act reviewed gives her the power to confer Syrian nationality ON her husband, in contrast to Kazakhstan and Montenegro's genuinely gender-neutral marriage routes built elsewhere in this dataset, and even worse than Lebanon/Senegal/Tanzania's asymmetric-but-existent husband-side routes (discretionary or reduced-residency, but present). This is disclosed as a confirmed structural absence, not a gap in sourcing. Separately, even the wife-side route is NOT unconditional: Article 18/19's Arab-nationality/Syrian-origin gate means a wife with no such background has no route modeled here at all (not found in the sections reviewed). dual_citizenship_allowed set null for the same reason as the descent file -- no explicit clause found in the sections reviewed.
